prompt:
This repository is Dispatch, an incident management platform. When an alert keeps going off and each repeat is folded into a case that is already open, Dispatch does not redraw the alert's post at the top of that case's chat thread for every single repeat. Which function decides whether a given repeat gets that post redrawn, and how much time must have passed since the last redraw for the same case before a repeat can trigger another one? Do not change any code.

Finish your answer with these three lines, in this exact form:
FILE: <path of the file that defines that function>
FUNCTION: <name of the function>
MIN_GAP: <the minimum time since the last redraw, number and unit>
notes: Answer: src/dispatch/signal/flows.py, _should_update_signal_message (called from signal_instance_create_flow when filter_signal filtered the instance): a repeat redraws the case's signal message only if its filter action is deduplicate, the case has a signal_thread_ts and at least timedelta(seconds=5) separates it from the instance that last triggered a redraw. Trap: the TTLCache next to it has ttl=60 (entries expire after 60 s, which also allows a redraw); update_signal_message does the redraw but does not decide. Lexical gap, grep -i on the fixture (src, tests, docs): 'redraw', 'going off', 'alert post', 'chat thread', 'decide' have 0 hits; 'folded' 1 (an icon name); 'repeat' 10 (icons, CSS, eslint, a Vue viewer); 'alert' 478 (mostly icons, the API schema and the unrelated data/alert module); 'thread' 268, 'trigger' 322, 'post' 2424. The code says signal, deduplicate, update, message, cache. Memory: an upstream detail from 2023 (#3337): a private helper and a 5-second constant inside a TTL-cached throttle, nothing a model recalls; the obvious guesses are update_signal_message or the 60 s TTL. No plant involved.
